events.title: Clang open-sourced
events.summary: Apple open-sourced Clang on July 11, 2007 — a C, C++, and [Objective-C] front end built on LLVM with fast diagnostics.
events.about: Clang compiles to LLVM IR with clearer error messages than GCC and powers Xcode, Swift, and many static analyzers. Its library design lets tools share the same parser — IDEs, linters, and formatters all ride one AST. Example: a typo in C++ template code gets a pinpoint note instead of pages of cascade errors.

narrative.whyChosen: Clang gave the LLVM ecosystem a modern, embeddable C-family compiler front end.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the default toolchain on macOS and influenced language tooling everywhere.
narrative.problemSolved: GCC's monolithic design made fast, friendly diagnostics and IDE integration difficult.
